data.body:
Fixed in Gerrit change 2002 (commit cd8fdb4622) — one file,
`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`, +29/-2, no behaviour change to what
either step checks.

## Diagnosis confirmed

Reproduced the mechanism exactly as described. `02f71da097` added both steps
AND created `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py`;
`git log --diff-filter=A` confirms the test file has no earlier provenance.

## Guard placement — one deliberate departure from "guard the step"

The first step names two scripts, and they have DIFFERENT vintages:

| script | added by | date |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` | `8c29eca552` | 2026-07-11 |
| `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` | `22efd71f10` | 2026-08-20 |

So I guarded them SEPARATELY rather than jointly. A joint "skip if either is
missing" guard would silence the `gen_cli_reference` check on every tree based
between those two dates — a five-week window of open changes — for no reason.
Two independent `if [ -f ... ]` blocks keep each check enforced exactly as far
back as its own script reaches.

That choice is also corroborated: `gen_cli_reference.py` is ALREADY gated with
this identical if-present shape in `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml`, so
old-base trees already run and pass it there. Guarding it jointly here would
have contradicted the treatment it already gets one directory over.

Wording matches the established form used by the comment-hygiene,
Verified-gate-parity and complexity-baseline gates, verbatim:
`"<path> not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping; the
gate re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change"`.

The dist-step guard is placed BEFORE the `pip install`, so an old-base tree
does no work at all rather than installing four packages and then skipping.

## Evidence — the guard fires AND does not suppress

Each step's `run:` block was extracted verbatim from the YAML and executed
under `bash -e` against real `git archive` trees. Both directions were tested,
because a guard that always skips would make the gate permanently silent.

NEGATIVE (guard fires):

| tree | condition | result |
|---|---|---|
| `22efd71f10^` | `gen_cli_help.py` absent | skip message printed; `gen_cli_reference.py` STILL RAN |
| `02f71da097^` | test file absent | skip message printed, exit 0 |

POSITIVE (guard does not suppress):

| tree | condition | result |
|---|---|---|
| `HEAD` | both generators present | both ran, exit 0 |
| `HEAD` | test file present | pytest collected 4 tests (not 0), exit 0 |
| `HEAD` + injected `assert False` | test file present but failing | exit 1 |
| `HEAD` + drifted `docs/cli-reference.md` | docs stale | exit 1, "docs/cli-reference.md is stale" |

The last two rows are the ones that matter: with the files present the steps
still FAIL on a violated contract, so the guard cannot be satisfied by never
running.

## One false alarm, chased down and dismissed

The first probe run showed `gen_cli_reference.py --check` FAILING on the
`22efd71f10^` tree, which would have meant the separate-guard decision
re-introduced the bug for that script. It was an artifact of my probe: the
worktree venv has an EDITABLE install, so `rebar` resolved from the CURRENT
`src/`, i.e. the OLD tree's generator was rendering the CURRENT package's help
text against the OLD tree's committed docs. Installing that tree's own rebar
into a throwaway venv and re-running gives exit 0 — the tree is
self-consistent. Real CI is self-consistent too: the step runs
`/tmp/clean/bin/python`, a venv holding a wheel built from the SAME tree.

## Gates

`make lint` (includes actionlint over all workflows, plus zizmor) clean;
`make typecheck` clean (618 files); `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`
24 passed. No full suite run — the host is heavily contended and a sweep tells
you nothing about a workflow guard.

## Scope held

No repo-wide guard sweep, no new CI check enforcing the guard pattern, no
change to what the steps check. I read the surrounding workflows while
confirming the diagnosis and did not find another unguarded script-invoking
step outside the two this bug names.

AC3 (a pre-`02f71da097`-based change passes the optionality lane) is
reconstructed rather than replayed: 1997/1998/1999 have since been rebased or
landed, so the equivalent reconstruction is the negative-case table above,
where the archived pre-`02f71da097` tree exercises the identical `run:` block
and skips instead of exiting 4.

Not closing until 2002 merges.
